clue.text: Give puzzler space to sharpen undiplomatic diplomacy?

parts.note: a request to give the setter something is 'give me', the puzzler being the setter speaking of themself
a gap is a space
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: A request that a baffled solver be given room to refine some tactless statecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Megaphone diplomacy' is the phrase for conducting relations by loud public statements rather than quiet negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Megaphone diplomacy is the idiom for loud, public, tactless dealings between states, so the device names that undiplomatic style.

clue.text: Bohemian girl's c-copy

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème, a Bohemian girl
the stammered first letter of the next word is simply C

explanation.surface: A stammering note about a girl from Bohemia owning a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'c-copy' supplies the final C, while the definition is the plain word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to imitate or ape them, which is to copy them.

clue.text: Welcome note to the Spanish inside protected area

indicators.note: says the note and the Spanish article sit within the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
NB, nota bene, is a written note to take notice
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A friendly message to Spanish speakers posted within a conservation zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' here is NB (nota bene), not a musical letter. A GREEN BELT is a ring of countryside round a British town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is land kept from development by planning rules, so it is an area under protection.

clue.text: Choice of money, when about to pass on

indicators.note: the coins are said to go round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: pence are British money
to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else

explanation.surface: Deciding which coins to hand on to somebody else.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option one favours, so it is a choice.

clue.text: Leaving home in time for fighting in ascent of 2 before spring

indicators.note: places the first part ahead of the word for spring
the time and the fighting are placed within the upturned pair
in a down entry, going up means the word for two is read bottom to top

parts.note: a duo is two
war is fighting
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Someone departing for war, climbing towards the second clue ahead of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is the number, not a reference to 2 Down: DUO climbs to OUD, and TWAR goes inside to make OUTWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or traveller setting off on a journey away from home is described as outward bound.

clue.text: Vibrator committing a murder?

indicators.note: the letters are being made to carry out, or be turned into, something else

explanation.surface: An instrument of vibration accused of killing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committing' signals the anagram of A MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates when sound waves strike it.

clue.text: See 4
Complaint of the glade in Innisfree?

definitions.meaning: Yeats's Lake Isle of Innisfree has a bee-loud glade; read bee plus F, the musical sign for loud

explanation.walkthrough: In W. B. Yeats's poem 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree' the poet lives 'alone in the bee-loud glade'; with F standing for forte, loud, bee-loud becomes BEE-F.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a complaint, and the poem's glade is bee-loud, BEE plus F for loud.

clue.text: Put off work till nearer heaven?

indicators.note: means the letters of the word put are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Procrastinating with a job until one is closer to the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes UPT from PUT; 'till' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up top means being high up, and so closer to the sky above.

clue.text: Mark out where to get the best food (unadulterated English)

parts.words: where to get the best food
parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells fine foods
neat spirits are unmixed, unadulterated

explanation.surface: Indicating where top-quality pure English food can be bought.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to trace or outline, so it is to mark out.

clue.text: 1,002 solvers? 17 nonsense!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, and the extra 2 doubles the solvers
ye is the old plural you, addressing the solvers
the second of the two solvers, again ye

explanation.surface: An exclamation dismissing a thousand-and-two puzzlers as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1,000 gives M and the 2 asks for two lots of YE. 17 is OPTICAL, so 'optical nonsense' is a jokey way of hinting at the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: My eye! is an old exclamation meaning rubbish or nonsense, and an eye is an optical organ.

clue.text: Heath plant, one left after wrong people got in

indicators.note: puts the remaining pieces following the first part
means the people are placed inside the word for wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A moorland herb, with one left behind after the wrong crowd broke in.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong, which a solver outside law may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered cinquefoil common on heaths and moors.

clue.text: Tin/lead alloy to support light ornaments

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: an alloy is a mixture, so the letters of lead are mixed up

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A tin and lead mixture used to hold up decorative lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alloy' makes DELA from LEAD; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Candelabra are ornamental branched holders for candles or lamps, hence ornaments carrying light.

clue.text: We showed recently that without minimal knowledge work comes to a stop

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: here means outside, so the work and stop wrap round the little knowledge

parts.note: an end is a stop
wee means tiny
ken is knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: A remark that, lacking even basic know-how, labour grinds to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We' is the Guardian, which had recently thrown open its offices to readers for a weekend event. OPEND is split after OPEN to take WEEKEN, leaving D at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper had lately hosted readers at its offices over a Saturday and Sunday, an event it billed under exactly this name.

clue.text: Make sure you get us a parliamentary waver

parts.note: to order something is to make sure you get it
the setter speaks for the Guardian, a newspaper

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy this newspaper, waved about in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs traditionally wave the ORDER PAPER, the day's printed agenda, to cheer in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The order paper lists a parliamentary day's business, and members wave it in the chamber, so it is a thing waved.

clue.text: See 12
Rodent to make love to bird outside church

parts.note: to woo is the old sense of to make love to, to court

indicators.note: the bird goes around the church, enclosing it

parts.note: a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: An animal courting a bird beyond the church walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make love to' is the old sense of courting, not anything racier.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodchuck, or groundhog, is a North American marmot, a burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Trouble in a tram from girl, one called Betty after 9 first

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Disturbance on a tram caused by a young woman known as Betty, coming after the earlier clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'all my eye and Betty Martin' (MY EYE is 9) means nonsense, so after 9 comes someone called Betty, MARTIN, plus A for one: a second route to the same girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Martina is a female forename, as with the tennis player Navratilova, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Tour Europe on line — land in 1-0

indicators.note: the land is placed within the scoreline words

parts.note: a one-nil score, I for one and NIL
terra is Latin for land, as in terra firma

explanation.surface: Travelling round Europe by railway and arriving in a one-nil scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: '1-0' is read as a football score, one-nil: I plus NIL, and TERRA goes inside NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrail is the pass that lets travellers roam Europe by train, so to interrail is to tour by line.

clue.text: Visual movement in a stone

indicators.note: the movement is set within the gemstone

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: An eye-catching motion seen inside a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or vision, so it means visual.

clue.text: Study in people's brief

indicators.note: the study is placed inside the word for people's

parts.note: laic means of the lay people rather than the clergy
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A short piece of research into a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, so it is terse and brief.

clue.text: Cover girl concealing warmth

indicators.note: the girl hides the warmth by enclosing it

parts.note: she is a female, a girl
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A model on a magazine front hiding how warm she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover girl' looks like one phrase, but 'Cover' is the definition and 'girl' gives SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to put it in its case, enclosing or covering it.

clue.text: Town has issue about air

indicators.note: the issue goes round the air, enclosing it

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring
wind is moving air

explanation.surface: A town whose offspring are concerned about the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: SWINDON is a large town in Wiltshire, England; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindon is an English railway town in Wiltshire, an example of a town.

clue.text: Copper with live figure

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A police officer with a lively build.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a solid three-dimensional shape, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Don't declare — stick

definitions.meaning: in cricket a side that does not declare its innings closed chooses to ...
a short stick, such as a relay runner's or a conductor's

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side may 'declare', ending its innings early; carrying on instead is to BAT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing to bat rather than declaring is batting on, and a baton is a stick.

clue.text: Dog very lively among geese, when not at home

indicators.note: the lively word sits in the middle of the geese
home is in, so the letters spelling in are removed

parts.note: a skein is a flight of wild geese
chipper means cheerful and lively

explanation.surface: A hound having a lively time among geese while away from its kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very lively' reads as two words of surface but together they mean chipper; the schipperke is a Belgian breed little known outside dog shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The schipperke is a small black Belgian breed of dog, once a barge dog.

clue.text: Dick on board?

definitions.meaning: Dick ... was a British television comedian
an ... board is a nail file coated with abrasive

explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a popular British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s; an emery board is a nail file.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's surname is the abrasive coating on a nail file, so both senses meet in one word.

clue.text: Married woman entertaining a neighbour

indicators.note: the married woman hosts the letter a within her title

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman

explanation.surface: A wife hosting a nearby resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the next planet out from Earth, so it is our planetary neighbour.

clue.text: Ill-natured in being spontaneous?

indicators.note: ill here means badly, so these letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone bad-tempered while being impulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-natured' looks like one word, but 'Ill' signals the anagram of NATURED IN; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour not shaped by training is natural and unrehearsed, which the question mark lets stand for spontaneous.

clue.text: Spot for catching fish?

indicators.note: catching means hearing, so the fish's name is heard

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A good location for landing fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a location or position, which a spot is.

clue.text: College in relation to grammar school?

parts.note: kin are relations

explanation.surface: A college linked to a selective state school.
explanation.walkthrough: King's is a college of Cambridge University; 'in' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: King's College is one of the Cambridge colleges, so the name stands for a college.

clue.text: Little money for meeting at heart

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A small sum offered for a gathering at the core.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed centrally is in the middle, the heart of a thing.
